p052.lead: From primitive man to the era of light and life: how the successive missions of the divine Sons divide the human history of a planet into seven epochs.

p052.foot.text: Sponsored by a Mighty Messenger temporarily attached to the staff of Gabriel

p052.s0.h: Introduction — Epochs Marked by the Visits of the Sons
p052.s0.b0: Paper 51 dealt with the Planetary Adams; Paper 52 widens the view to the whole human history of an evolutionary planet. From the time life begins until it flowers in the era of light and life, at least seven epochs appear. What divides these epochs is neither technology nor dynasty but the **planetary missions of the divine Sons**.

p052.s0.b3: The span from the initiation of life to the appearance of man is set apart as the prehuman era and comes before the mortal epochs this paper describes. Throughout, the paper also draws a contrast: the order of a normal world, and Urantia’s situation, thrown out of that order by rebellion and isolation. So the paper is both a map of the future and a mirror held up to our own world.
p052.s1.h: I. Primitive Man — A Long, Dark, Yet Heroic Chapter
p052.s1.b0: From the time man emerges from the animal level and can choose to worship the Creator until the arrival of the Planetary Prince, mortals are called primitive men. Six colored races appear in the order of the spectrum, beginning with the red; the law of this age is the physical survival of the fittest, and government is wholly tribal. People live in caves or on cliffs and learn to kindle fire, and on some planets they are helped by enormous birds that can carry a man nonstop for over five hundred miles.
p052.s1.b2: The religion of this age is largely animal fear mixed with ignorant awe and tribal superstition. Yet the paper does not simply disparage it. Fear religion subdues fiery tempers and becomes the soil in which the Planetary Prince later plants the seeds of revealed religion. Once will appears, the temporary indwelling of Adjusters begins, and within a hundred thousand years of man’s standing erect the Planetary Prince usually arrives.
p052.s2.h: II. Post-Planetary Prince Man — The Golden Age of the Home Begins
p052.s2.b0: With the arrival of the Planetary Prince, government appears and a new dispensation opens, averaging around five hundred thousand years. The prince and his staff give the first revelations of higher truth and universe organization, and from then on religion grows along two paths together: evolutionary growth and graduated revelation. But the prince is not yet the Prince of Peace, and racial dispersion and intense nationalism reach their peak in this age.
p052.s2.b2: As the idea of family grows, the roving life of the hunter gives way to settled homes and agriculture, and normal worlds establish full equality of the sexes. The paper also says that normal worlds take up the task of race purification in this period, restricting the multiplication of defective strains. At the same time it adds that there is abundant opportunity to show tolerance and altruism toward unfortunate individuals who have not lost their moral heritage.
p052.s2.b3: Religiously, this age is a spiritual dawn. Running through all the racial religions are two strains: the fears of primitive man and the revelations of the Planetary Prince. The paper remarks that in some respects Urantians do not seem to have wholly emerged from this stage. Telling apart faith born of fear and faith born of revelation remains a task for readers today.
p052.s3.h: III. Post-Adamic Man — An Age of Invention and Internationalism
p052.s3.b0: When man reaches the highest level biologically possible, a Material Son and Daughter sent by the System Sovereign arrive. The prime purpose of the Adamic regime is to move civilization from the hunter and herder stage to that of the agriculturist and horticulturist. The gift of Adam’s life plasm raises intellectual capacity and quickens spiritual progress, and on an average world this becomes a golden age of invention, energy control, and exploration.
p052.s3.b2: By the end of the Adamic age the races are practically blended, taking on an olive shade of the violet hue, the racial “white” of the spheres. Nationalism wanes, representative government replaces monarchy, education becomes world-wide, and a common language takes hold. The paper holds that universal peace is seldom attained until the races are blended and speak a common tongue.
p052.s4.h: IV. Post-Magisterial Son Man — A Society That Knows How to Use Leisure
p052.s4.b0: To a world whose races are blended and at peace comes an Avonal Son from Paradise on a magisterial mission. Unlike the Planetary Prince and the Material Sons, who are of local universe origin, the Magisterial Son hails from Paradise, and on his first magisterial mission he is incarnated without experiencing birth or death. If one mission is not enough, a second or a series of Magisterial Sons follows, and each advent marks the end of one dispensation and the beginning of the next.
p052.s4.b2: In this age two and one-half hours of daily work are enough to sustain one’s independence, and self-government becomes established. Interestingly, toward the end of the age society begins to return to simpler ways of living. The physical sciences have already reached their height; art, music, and higher learning flower; and a world-wide spiritual awakening signals the coming of the bestowal Son. The insight here is that leisure becomes liberation only when ethical maturity to use it comes first.
p052.s4.b3: In this epoch the majority of mortals are indwelt by Thought Adjusters, but Adjusters of fusion destiny are not yet bestowed on all; it is still necessary for will creatures to choose the Mystery Monitors. The greater God’s gift becomes, the weightier the human choice to receive it.
p052.s5.h: V. Post-Bestowal Son Man — The New and Living Way
p052.s5.b0: When a world becomes ripe for spiritualization, a bestowal Son of the Avonal order arrives. The exception occurs once in each local universe, when the Creator Son makes his terminal bestowal—as when Michael appeared on Urantia. On normal worlds the bestowal Son comes when intellectual and ethical attainment is highest, but on Urantia he appeared at the close of the Adamic dispensation.
p052.s5.b2: On Urantia the establishment of this way was a matter of fact as well as truth. After the Lucifer rebellion, the procedure by which mortals pass directly to the mansion worlds at death had been suspended; since Pentecost, Urantia mortals may again proceed directly to the morontia spheres. When the bestowal Son ascends, the Spirit of Truth is poured out upon all flesh, the bestowal edict of the Adjusters is issued, and every normal-minded will creature receives an Adjuster on reaching the age of moral choice.

p052.s6.h: VI. Urantia’s Post-Bestowal Age — Five Paths to Brotherhood
p052.s6.b0: On a normal world the age after the bestowal Son is a dispensation of world-wide peace, but not on Urantia. Jesus himself warned of “⟦Q 52:6.1⟧wars and rumors of wars⟦/Q⟧.” Because unaided social evolution can hardly achieve brotherhood on an isolated planet, the paper says religious revelation is essential, and it sets out five conditions for social brotherhood.

p052.s6.b4: Before they are grand planetary programs, these five conditions are personal tasks. Reading the literature of another culture, choosing emotional maturity over selfish calculation, seeing a neighbor as a child of the same Father—one person can begin these today. The paper says the quickest way is the spiritual transformation of humanity.
p052.s7.h: VII. Post-Teacher Son Man — The Threshold of Light and Life
p052.s7.b0: Next the Trinity Teacher Sons come, in groups. A planetary Teacher Son is supported by seventy primary Sons, twelve secondary Sons, and three of the most experienced Daynals, and the corps remains for at least a thousand years. Urantia is out of step here too, because Jesus promised to return, and no one knows when that second coming will take place in relation to the other Sons.
p052.s7.b1: In this age more and more Adjusters fuse with their subjects during the life in the flesh, natural death becomes less frequent, and the length of life approaches five hundred years. Representative government vanishes and the rule of individual self-control begins; about an hour a day from each adult is enough for the physical administration of the world. Still, the paper makes clear that the inhabitants remain finite and mortal, and nothing is perfect.
p052.s7.b3: The greatest comfort is that this final prospect is open to every world. Whether a realm has been wholly loyal, tainted with evil, or cursed by sin, sooner or later the grace of God and the ministry of angels will usher in the day of the Teacher Sons and begin the era of light and life. Backward Urantia is no exception.
p052.s8.b0: Paper 52 teaches us to read history as a course of education carried forward by divine visitations. Each epoch opens only on the soil prepared by the one before, and revelation expands only as far as a world can receive it. Urantia has departed from the normal order in many ways, yet the paper’s conclusion is not discouragement but hope. Brotherhood and peace are a story about distant planets, and also work each of us can help with now.

p052.s8.b2: Papers 53 and 54 turn squarely to the cause of Urantia’s departure from the normal order: the Lucifer rebellion and the problems it left behind. Keeping this picture of a normal world in mind makes it clearer what the rebellion took away.
p053.lead: How a brilliant System Sovereign surrendered to the sophistry of self-assertion: the causes, course, and present status of the Lucifer rebellion.

p053.foot.text: Presented by Manovandet Melchizedek, onetime attached to the receivership of Urantia

p053.s0.h: Introduction — The Fall of the Most Brilliant
p053.s0.b0: Paper 52 described the normal sequence of planetary epochs; Paper 53 turns to the root of Urantia’s departure from it. Lucifer was no ordinary being. He was a brilliant primary Lanonandek Son of Nebadon, designated one of the hundred most able and brilliant personalities among more than seven hundred thousand of his kind, and he was chief executive of the system of Satania with its 607 inhabited worlds.
p053.s0.b2: Of the ten thousand systems of Nebadon, only three System Sovereigns have ever been found in contempt of the Creator Son’s government. This paper asks us to read the rebellion not as a legend of a distant heaven but as a warning: even a personality of great gifts and high position can fall through pride and self-deception.
p053.s1.b0: Little was heard of Lucifer on Urantia, because he assigned his first lieutenant, Satan, to advocate his cause on this planet. The paper sorts out, one by one, names that tradition has blended together.

p053.s1.b3: The universe’s attitude toward the rebel is worth noticing. Before Michael’s bestowal, subordinate intelligences showed Lucifer neither disrespect nor disdain, and even Michael’s archangel did not accuse him but left judgment to the Judge; such judgment belongs to the Ancients of Days. Here we see a restraint that leaves condemnation to rightful authority and refuses to mock even one who has done wrong.
p053.s2.h: II. The Causes of Rebellion — Within the Mind, Not Without
p053.s2.b0: There were no special conditions in Satania that favored rebellion, and no one ever suggested it to Lucifer. His relations with the Creator Son had been intimate and cordial. The author believes the idea took origin in Lucifer’s own mind and that he might have stirred up rebellion wherever he had been stationed.
p053.s2.b1: The process unfolded in stages. First pride grew until it became self-deception, and Lucifer persuaded himself that rebellion was for the good of the system. By the time his plans reached disillusionment, he had gone too far for his pride to let him stop, and at some point evil became deliberate and willful sin. He was long offered the chance to repent, but he rejected Michael’s mercy with increasing contempt.
p053.s2.b3: This analysis applies just as well to our own inner life. Great wrongs seldom arrive suddenly. First comes a season of professing loyalty outwardly while nursing criticism and discontent inwardly, and only after many missed chances to turn back does a deliberate choice harden.
p053.s3.h: III. The Lucifer Manifesto — Three Charges
p053.s3.b0: The rebellion finally took form as the Lucifer Declaration of Liberty. Its case was stated under three heads, and each one flatly denies a central truth taught in the earlier papers of The Urantia Book.

head: Charge
Lucifer’s claim
rows: 1. The reality of the Universal Father
The Father does not exist; he is a myth invented by the Paradise Sons. Personality is not the Father’s gift.
2. The universe government of the Creator Son
Local systems should be autonomous. The Ancients of Days are meddling tyrants, and immortality is inherent in system personalities.
3. The plan of ascendant mortal training
The long training is wasted on a fictitious destiny. Ascenders should enjoy individual self-determination.

p053.s3.b3: The declaration was wrapped in attractive words. Liberty, self-government, and equality are precious values in themselves. But the moment they are cut off from the Father and from universe order, they become sophistry. The same words can serve truth or plot rebellion, and so this manifesto remains a test of discernment for readers today.
p053.s4.h: IV–V. Outbreak of the Rebellion; Nature of the Conflict
p053.s4.b0: The manifesto was issued about two hundred thousand years ago, Urantia time, at the annual conclave of Satania on the sea of glass. Self-assertion was the battle cry, and Lucifer proclaimed “⟦Q 53:4.2⟧equality of mind⟦/Q⟧,” “majorities rule,” and “⟦Q 53:4.4⟧mind is infallible.⟦/Q⟧” He even pointed to the merciful delays of justice as proof that the universe government was powerless.
p053.s4.b2: After conferring with Immanuel, Michael adopted a policy of noninterference. Having not yet completed his bestowal career, he did not yet rule in his own personal right, and Gabriel took command of the loyal hosts. The so-called “⟦Q 53:5.6⟧war in heaven⟦/Q⟧” was not a physical battle but a debate, in which personalities journeyed back and forth between Lucifer’s harangues and Gabriel’s exposures until they made up their own minds.

p053.s4.b5: Gabriel displayed Michael’s banner on the sphere dedicated to the very Universal Father whose personality Lucifer and Satan had questioned. The two years and more of confusion that followed were a great trial for the loyal. The most distinctive feature of this conflict is that instead of immediate suppression, time was given for every being to choose freely.
p053.s5.h: VI. A Loyal Seraphic Commander — Manotia
p053.s5.b0: When the head of the Jerusem seraphic hosts went over to Lucifer, Manotia, second in command, refused to join the insult to Michael. With the system circuits cut, he held on until the new Sovereign arrived, upheld morally by the Melchizedeks and helped by the Material Sons and the ascendant mortals. He saved almost two thirds of the administrator seraphim.
p053.s5.b1: Manotia’s account also contains a keen observation about why the lower angels fell. They simply could not grasp that so dazzling a personality could go wrong. The lesson is that discernment collapses when we confuse a person’s charm and authority with truth itself.
p053.s6.h: VII. History of the Rebellion — Who Fell and Who Stood
p053.s6.b0: The rebellion spread throughout the system. Thirty-seven Planetary Princes seceded, but on Panoptia a young woman named Ellanora took the lead of the human races, and not a single soul enlisted under Lucifer’s banner. Satania was isolated from the constellation and universe circuits, and those circuits will not be restored so long as the archrebel lives within Satania.

p053.s6.b3: The most striking line in this table is the last. What Lucifer mocked most fiercely was the plan of ascendant mortal training, yet the mortals schooled by that very plan stood the most firmly. The assurance went on to Paradise that the survival experience of mortal ascension is the surest safeguard against sin.
p053.s6.b4: After the new Sovereign, Lanaforge, arrived, the rebels lost all governing powers but were allowed to go freely about the system. Even so, in almost two hundred thousand years they have not deceived another world. Since the fall of the thirty-seven, no Satania world has been lost.
p053.s7.h: VIII. The Son of Man on Urantia
p053.s7.b0: Lucifer and Satan roamed Satania freely until Michael completed his bestowal, and they were last on this world together during their combined assault upon the Son of Man. When Jesus answered, “⟦Q 53:8.4⟧Get you behind me, Satan⟦/Q⟧,” there was survival for mortals and security for angels; in principle, that was the real end of the rebellion.
p053.s7.b2: This section lifts away fear. Since Pentecost, Caligastia and Daligastia are servile before the Adjusters and the Spirit of Truth, and no fallen spirit ever had the power to invade the minds of the children of God. What is often blamed on devils is usually the result of people being led away by their own tendencies. So rather than blaming evil spirits outside us, we do better to examine our own choices.
p053.s8.h: IX. Present Status of the Rebellion
p053.s8.b0: From the early days of the rebellion Michael offered forgiveness and reinstatement to all who sincerely repented. None of the leaders accepted, but thousands of angels and hundreds of Material Sons and Daughters accepted the mercy and were rehabilitated at the time of Jesus’ resurrection. Lucifer is a prisoner on a satellite of the Jerusem transition spheres, and Satan too is now unqualifiedly detained. All await the Uversa verdict in the case of Gabriel vs. Lucifer.
p053.s8.b1: Satan could once come to Urantia because no Son of standing resided here—neither Planetary Prince nor Material Son. Since then Machiventa Melchizedek has been proclaimed vicegerent Planetary Prince, and the opening of the case of Gabriel vs. Lucifer signaled temporary planetary regimes on all the isolated worlds. The author believes that every rebel who will ever accept mercy has done so, and he awaits the broadcast by which the traitors will “⟦Q 53:9.7⟧become as though they had not been.⟦/Q⟧”
p053.s9.b0: Paper 53 locates the origin of evil not in some outside fate but in the choice of a personality. The rebellion began in pride, passed through self-deception, and hardened into deliberate sin, while mercy was offered again and again and refused. By contrast, those who stayed loyal through the trial—above all the seasoned ascending mortals—showed that faith and training are the surest shield.

p054.lead: True and false liberty, and why justice was delayed so long: a paper that answers, from the standpoint of love, the questions the Lucifer rebellion left behind.

p054.foot.text: Presented by a Mighty Messenger of experiential survival in the first system rebellion in the universes of time

p054.s0.h: Introduction — Telling Evil, Error, Sin, and Iniquity Apart
p054.s0.b0: Paper 53 recorded the course of the Lucifer rebellion; Paper 54 takes up the philosophical questions it raised. The author is a Mighty Messenger who lived through a rebellion himself and survived. He begins by noting that evolutionary man finds it hard to grasp the meanings of evil, error, sin, and iniquity, and so he starts by distinguishing these four words clearly.

head: Concept
Where it arises
What constitutes it
rows: A universe with differential levels of perfection

p054.s0.b3: This distinction helps us see our own faults clearly. Being imperfect is not in itself sin; it is the unavoidable condition of a growing universe. Sin begins with a choice made knowingly, and iniquity hardens when that choice is persisted in.
p054.s1.b0: Of all the problems that grew out of the rebellion, none caused more difficulty than the failure to distinguish true liberty from false. True liberty is the reward of long evolutionary progress and rests on the reality of justice—intelligence, maturity, fraternity, and equity. Liberty that is unintelligent, unconditioned, and uncontrolled, by contrast, becomes a self-destroying technique.

False liberty
rows: Tends toward exploiting others for selfish aggrandizement
Compatible with the reign of love and the ministry of mercy

p054.s1.b3: The central principle of this section is that liberty does not exist in a vacuum. Cut off from material justice, intellectual fairness, social forbearance, moral duty, and spiritual values, it destroys itself. And when the Supreme Rulers of the universe themselves stand back in respect for the creature’s will, no being has the right to rob his fellows of their rights in the name of his own liberty.
p054.s1.b5: The author says there is no greater error than the self-deception that makes intelligent beings crave power over others in order to take away their natural liberties; the golden rule cries out against all such fraud and injustice. He adds that on a primitive world people may have to fight tyrants and oppressors for their material liberties, but on worlds of normal advancing civilization physical combat has long since fallen into disrepute. As a civilization matures, the struggle for liberty moves from weapons to fairness.
p054.s2.b0: Ever since God projected Havona with the Son and in the Spirit, the eternal pattern of shared participation in creation has held. Every creature of an evolving universe who aspires to do the Father’s will is destined to become a partner of the Creators in the adventure of experiential perfection. Were this not so, the Father would hardly have given such creatures free will or come to indwell them.
p054.s2.b1: Seen this way, Lucifer’s declaration was not an enlargement of liberty but a theft of it. His folly was trying to short-circuit time in an experiential universe; his crime was trying to rob every personality of the joy of contributing something of its own to the long struggle toward light and life. Dressed in the garments of liberty, it would actually have taken from men and angels the divine privilege of helping to create their own destinies.
p054.s3.h: III–IV. The Time Lag of Justice; The Mercy Time Lag
p054.s3.b0: People ask why the all-wise Creators permit evil and sin. The author’s answer is plain: both are inevitable if the creature is to be truly free. The ability to choose good or evil is not a philosophic symbol but a universe reality, and the Supreme Rulers will not let any being take this liberty from a single personality.
p054.s3.b1: There is a further reason for the delay of justice. Even though wholehearted identification with sin amounts in the end to annihilation, enough time must pass between that point and the execution of the penalty for the verdict to be recognized as fair by all concerned—even by the sinner himself. The Ancients of Days annihilate no one until all moral values are extinct in the evildoer and in his possible sympathizers.
p054.s3.b2: The delay of mercy can be understood with a parent’s heart. Like the father in Jesus’ story of the prodigal son, a loving father can wait long for an erring child to repent. If extended mercy might lead to repentance and rehabilitation, any length of delay in executing justice is justified.
p054.s3.b3: Ironically, Lucifer already had most of the liberties he demanded, and the rest he was to receive in the future. He lost these precious gifts by yielding to impatience—to wanting what he craved now—and by disregarding his obligation to respect the rights of every other being. Impatience does not bring the gift sooner; it makes us lose it.
p054.s3.b5: Nor do these delays go on forever. While this revelation was being made, the first hearing of the case of Gabriel vs. Lucifer was held on Uversa, and soon afterward the Ancients of Days ordered Satan confined to the prison world with Lucifer, so that he can no longer visit the fallen worlds.
p054.s3.b7: This delay is also the saving interval between seedtime and harvest. If the seed is good, the interval tests and builds character; if it is evil, it gives time for repentance and correction. When reward or punishment does not come at once in our own lives, we need neither lose heart nor grow careless; that time is room for grace.
p054.s4.h: V. The Wisdom of Delay — Twelve Reasons Permitted to Be Told
p054.s4.b0: The author lists the reasons he knows and is permitted to recite. On Uversa, he says, forty-eight reasons are taught for allowing evil to run the full course of its own moral bankruptcy and spiritual extinction, and he suspects there are as many more unknown to him.

p054.s4.b2: Two points stand out in this list. First, evil that is hastily covered over does not disappear; it lingers in hiding. Only when rebellion is fully exposed can every being see it clearly and decide for himself. Second, our impatience with time is a matter of perspective: what seems a long delay to us may be very brief in a wider view.
p054.s4.b4: The explanation of the Paradise emergency adviser deserves special notice. Unless every creature of Norlatiadek had full and free opportunity to choose, the Paradise quarantine against halfhearted or doubt-stricken creatures would have had to be extended to the whole constellation. The delay, then, was not leniency toward rebels; it was a measure to keep the doors of ascension open to all, the loyal included. The entire Uversa corps of counselors likewise advised letting the rebellion take its natural course, even if it took a million years to wind up the consequences.
p054.s5.b0: The final section says that the whole manner of dealing with the rebellion is a vindication of divine love. The Creator Son and the Paradise Father are love dominated in all their dealings with intelligent beings, and God as a Father takes precedence over every other phase of Deity. Without remembering this, we cannot understand the attitude of the universe rulers toward the rebels.
p054.s5.b1: Of course, the innocent suffer because of mercy’s delay. Families, nations, worlds, and systems are all relationships of association, so their members profit from one another’s right conduct and also bear the consequences of one another’s wrongdoing. But the author offers an eternal assurance that such hardships are only temporary.
p054.s5.b3: Further, the rebellion eventually brought forth good. The Jerusem citizens who withstood the test advanced in status and spiritual worth, and the Melchizedeks now teach that the good resulting from the Satania rebellion is more than a thousand times the sum of all the evil. The sum of evil has become almost stationary, while its beneficial repercussions keep spreading, even to Havona. Yet this harvest was possible only because Lucifer’s superiors took a wise and merciful attitude.
p054.s5.b4: This does not justify evil as a tool for good. Good cannot come of evil to the one who contemplates and performs it; but all things work together for good to those who know God and love to do his will. And the ability to decline survival did not begin with the rebellion; it has always been part of man’s gift of free will.
p054.s6.b0: Paper 54 binds liberty, justice, and mercy into one picture. True liberty grows within self-control and brotherhood, justice waits to give mercy time to save, and the Father’s love presides over the whole process. The author admits that he himself fully understood these complexities only after serving in superuniverse administration. So it is no shame that we do not understand everything now; it is the natural course of the ascent.

p054.s6.b2: Paper 55 lifts our gaze from the shadow of rebellion far into the future, picturing the spheres of light and life that evolutionary planets finally attain. There we see the goal toward which this merciful delay is moving.
p055.lead: Morontia temples, translation in place of death, a golden age funded by the tithe: the final goal of an evolutionary planet and its seven stages.

p055.foot.text: Presented by a Mighty Messenger temporarily assigned to the Archangel Council on Urantia

p055.s0.h: Introduction — The Summit of Evolution, Yet a Beginning
p055.s0.b0: Paper 52 followed the planetary epochs from primitive man to the age of the Teacher Sons; Paper 55 pictures the era of light and life that lies at the end of that road. It begins when the Teacher Sons conclude their final mission and continues indefinitely on the inhabited worlds, and as far as the author knows, worlds so settled are destined to go on throughout all future eternal ages.

p055.s0.b3: An important qualification is added. These stages are described in terms of universe organization, but any world may attain the planetary values of any stage quite independently of the development of other worlds. The same is true of individuals: our growth is not blocked because those around us lag behind.
p055.s1.h: I. The Morontia Temple — The Certificate of Light and Life
p055.s1.b0: The appearance of a morontia temple at the planetary capital is the certificate that a world has entered light and life. On that day the planet’s Paradise bestowal Son comes in person and proclaims the long-serving Planetary Prince as Planetary Sovereign. The temple has three parts: at the center, the sanctuary of the bestowal Son; on the right, the seat of the Planetary Sovereign; on the left, the seat of the acting chief of finaliters.
p055.s1.b2: The temple is said to “come down from heaven,” but no material is actually transported; it is built on the planet from a miniature design worked out on the system capital. Seating about three hundred thousand, it is used not for worship or play but for communication with the System Sovereign, silent cosmic contemplation, graduation exercises and recognition of service, and above all as the place to witness the translation of living mortals.
p055.s2.h: II. Death and Translation — Where Funerals Become Graduations
p055.s2.b1: As a planet advances, more and more mortals fuse with their Adjusters and pass alive into the morontia state. By the terminal mission of the Teacher Sons about one quarter escape natural death, and by the fourth stage more than half leave by translation. When fusion approaches, a summons is issued; the candidate resigns his duties, bids farewell, and waits in the morontia temple, surrounded by family and friends, for the translation flash.
p055.s2.b3: The author says it would help if less advanced mortals could learn to view natural death with something of this same cheerfulness. Souls translated in this way bypass the mansion worlds and go straight to the universe headquarters, but ascenders who did not have that experience are given the chance on the seven mansion spheres to learn everything they missed. The universe applies equalizing techniques so that no ascender is deprived of anything essential to the ascent.
p055.s3.h: III. The Golden Ages — Not Perfect, Yet Heaven on Earth
p055.s3.b0: In this era the world moves forward with one language, one religion, and, on normal spheres, one race. Yet the author makes clear that the age is not perfect. There are still hospitals; accidents and the infirmities of old age must still be cared for; disease has not been entirely vanquished. Even so, were we transported there, we would call it heaven on earth.

p055.s3.b2: The way this first-stage world the author visited finances its public life reveals the community’s values. Natural resources are administered as community property, the highest honor is the order of “supreme service,” and most social and judicial posts are held jointly by men and women. That even such a world still presents plenty of evil, real and potential, to stimulate choice tells us that virtue does not arise automatically; it is still grown by choosing.
p055.s4.h: IV. Administrative Readjustments — Finaliters Return to Serve
p055.s4.b0: A settled world advances under the administration of the volunteer Corps of the Finality, ascenders who reached Paradise and came back to serve their brethren in the flesh. In the first stage the Planetary Sovereign, the chief of finaliters, and Adam and Eve, who unify the two, govern together, with the liberated midwayers serving as interpreters. Counselors are added stage by stage, and Adam and Eve are finally released from planetary duty and choose one of five careers.
p055.s4.b1: In the third or fourth stage an elected mortal chief executive appears and serves with the Planetary Sovereign for twenty-five years of planetary time. The ministering-spirit quartette that assists him never offers counsel unless asked. It is striking how these higher beings stand back out of respect for human self-direction.
p055.s4.b2: One of the last acts of the Teacher Sons on their terminal mission is to liberate the midwayers and give them responsible places in the new administration. Thanks to the final discoveries of physical science, mortals can now recognize these cousins, invisible since the early Adamic regime. Those who served unseen for so long are at last acknowledged as fellows.

p055.s5.h: V–VI. The Acme of Material Development; The Individual Mortal
p055.s5.b0: On worlds in the advanced stages, poverty and social inequality have all but vanished, war is a matter of history, and there are no armies or police. Self-control is rendering human laws obsolete, and the schools are devoted to training the mind and expanding the soul. Life is refreshingly simple, and the pursuit of happiness is an experience of joy and satisfaction.
p055.s5.b2: The people there become more altruistic and fraternal without losing their independence or devotion to family. Still, they are mortals who breathe, eat, and sleep; this world is not heaven but a foreshadowing of the divine worlds of the ascent. The author conjectures that there can never be a limit to intellectual evolution and the attainment of wisdom.
p055.s5.b3: Spiritual growth continues as well. Mortals commune ever more deeply with the indwelling Father fragment, and the ministry of the Holy Spirit and the angels grows more effective with each epoch. In the fourth stage, advanced mortals seem to experience considerable conscious contact with the Master Spirit of their superuniverse, and their philosophy focuses on understanding new revelations of God the Supreme.
p055.s6.h: VII–X. From the Planet to the Local Universe
p055.s6.b0: In the first stage the outwardly visible rulers are the Planetary Adam and Eve, and it is this arrangement that gave prestige to the idea of kings and queens throughout the universe. The author says that when Urantia reaches this era, Machiventa Melchizedek, now vicegerent Planetary Prince, will no doubt occupy the seat of Planetary Sovereign. When the youngest world of a system has been settled for a millennium, the whole system enters the second stage.
p055.s6.b1: In the system stage a legislative assembly is formed, with ten representatives from each planet, and the System Sovereign no longer changes. In the constellation stage the Most Highs are exalted to their true dignity, and in the local universe stage a supreme council of unlimited authority, made up of one hundred Faithfuls of Days, is established. Only then does the finaliter corps for the first time acknowledge an authority this side of Paradise.
p055.s6.b2: Once a local universe is settled, the Creator Son becomes administratively free and spends much time counseling the finaliter groups, and Michael finds fuller fraternity with glorified mortals. The author refrains from speculating about the Creator Sons’ role in the outer universes, yet he is sure that if they go, the Divine Ministers will go with them, and that the Melchizedeks will remain in their universes of origin.
p055.s7.h: XI–XII. From the Sectors to the Superuniverse — A Future No One Has Yet Seen
p055.s7.b0: Not one of the seven superuniverses has yet been settled in light and life. So the author says again and again, with humility, that about the fifth and later stages “⟦Q 55:12.5⟧we really do not know.⟦/Q⟧” The settling of the whole grand universe will be the most profound event since the appearance of the central universe, and some hold that the Supreme Being will then emerge as the experiential sovereign of the perfected creation.
p055.s7.b1: The greatest comfort in this section concerns the individual. The administrative machinery of a universe cannot limit or retard the spiritual progress of an individual planet or mortal. Even on an isolated world, environmental limitations cannot thwart personal attainment.
p055.s8.b0: Paper 55 is a distant landscape showing where our world is heading. A society in which death becomes a graduation, law gives way to self-control, and income is shared for truth, beauty, and goodness still seems far away. Yet through the life of Jesus the paper confirms that this status can be attained personally, by one person, even on an isolated world.

p055.s8.b2: Paper 56 turns to the principle that binds all this progress together: universal unity across the physical, intellectual, spiritual, and personal levels. The era of light and life is, in the end, that unity made real on a single world.
p056.lead: God is unity: from the unification of the physical, mind, spirit, and personality to truth, beauty, goodness, and love, the paper that closes Part II by binding the universe into one.

p056.foot.text: Presented by a Mighty Messenger visiting on Urantia, in collaboration with a certain Melchizedek, the vicegerent Planetary Prince of Urantia

p056.s0.b0: Paper 56 is the last paper of Part II, which deals with the local universe. Where the earlier papers introduced the Sons and the spirits, the angels and the planetary ages one by one, this paper declares the principle that binds them all together. The physical, intellectual, and spiritual domains are divinely correlated, and that is why a finite creature can ascend to Paradise.
p056.s0.b2: To the limited vision of mortals, the universe often seems disharmonious and poorly co-ordinated. But the more widely we observe, and the better we learn to detect the basic unity beneath creative diversity, the more clearly we perceive one divine purpose in every manifestation of energy. This paper is an exercise in cultivating that vision.

head: Dimension of unity
Center
Unifying agency
rows: The Isle of Paradise, the person of the Universal Father
Gravity, the Unqualified Absolute and the Deity Absolute
Cosmic mind, the Seven Master Spirits
The spirit-gravity circuit, the Divine Ministers

p056.s1.h: I. Physical Co-ordination — All Forces from One Source
p056.s1.b0: The material creation is not infinite, but it is perfectly co-ordinated. There are force, energy, and power, yet all are one in origin. The superuniverses seem dual and the central universe triune, but Paradise is single. The Unqualified Absolute upholds the physical universe, the Deity Absolute motivates its overcontrol, and the two are unified in the Universal Absolute.
p056.s1.b1: The point of this section is that duality does not exist within the Father’s infinite nature. The division between physical and spiritual appears only when we look aside from his infinite level. And to bridge that divergence, mind is indispensable.
p056.s1.b3: Gravity unification is universal and unvarying, and pure energy and pure spirit are wholly preresponsive to gravity. Because these primal forces are personally controlled by the Father, all gravity finally centers in his personal presence. The hidden comfort of this section is that at the very bottom of the forces holding the universe together there stands not an impersonal law but a Person.
p056.s2.b0: The Father’s primal thought is eternalized in a dual expression—the Isle of Paradise and the Eternal Son—and this duality makes the mind God, the Infinite Spirit, inevitable. Cosmic mind extends from the primitive ministry of the adjutant spirits to the magnificent mind of a universe’s chief executive, yet it is unified under the Seven Master Spirits.
p056.s2.b2: The same is true of spirit. As mind gravity centers in the Infinite Spirit, spirit gravity centers in the Eternal Son. In time and space, spirit appears in three ways: the spirit personalities of the Eternal Son, the spirit personalities associated with the Infinite Spirit, and pure-spirit fragments such as the Thought Adjusters, the Father’s bestowal. These three spirit endowments become perfectly unified at last in the finaliters.
p056.s2.b3: This is also something that happens within us. The mortal mind is the creation of the children of the Son and the Spirit, and when it fuses with the Adjuster it shares in the threefold spirit endowment. When our thinking and our spiritual longing seem at odds, it has practical meaning to know that it is the ministry of mind that joins the two.
p056.s3.h: IV. Personality Unification — No Child Has Two Fathers
p056.s3.b0: The Universal Father is a divinely unified personality, and so all his ascending children will likewise be fully unified personalities before they reach Havona. Personality inherently reaches out to unify all its constituent realities, and because the personality of mortal man is a direct bestowal of the Father, it has the potential to unify body, mind, and spirit.
p056.s3.b2: Philosophically we may, and must, conceive of plural levels of Deity and even plural Trinities. But in the experience of worship, God is always one—our Paradise parent. However complex the cosmology we learn, the one who prays can return to the simple relationship of Father and child.
p056.s4.h: V–VI. Deity Unity; Unification of Evolutionary Deity
p056.s4.b0: The oneness of Paradise Deity is existential and absolute. There are three personalizations, yet in the Trinity they are one undivided Deity. In the evolving universes, things are different: the first three levels of God the Sevenfold—the Creator Sons and Creative Spirits, the Ancients of Days, and the Seven Master Spirits—are being co-ordinated in the Supreme Being.
p056.s4.b2: On any level, God cannot exceed the conceptual capacity of the beings on that level. So mortals come to know the God of love by recognizing truth, appreciating beauty, and worshiping goodness, and then progress through ascending Deity levels to comprehension of the Supreme. That even the finaliters have not yet found the Supreme Being shows how long this journey is.
p056.s5.h: VII–VIII. Universal Evolutionary Repercussions; The Supreme Unifier
p056.s5.b0: Each time a world, system, constellation, or universe reaches the height of evolutionary progress, Deity function expands in that unit, with repercussions in every other realm. When a system is settled in light, the Son-Spirit liaison reaches its fullness of function; when a local universe is completed, the ministry of the Master Spirits becomes more direct. About what will happen in the outer universes, the author says again and again, “⟦Q 56:7.6⟧We do not know⟦/Q⟧.”

What it means for mortals

p056.s5.b2: Finaliters are born in the local universes, nurtured in the superuniverses, and trained in the central universe, and then serve in turn in superuniverses other than their own, gathering the full sevenfold range of creature experience. Through the Adjusters they find the Father, but it is by these techniques of experience that they come to know the Supreme Being, and they are destined to serve and reveal him in the outer universes of the future.
p056.s5.b4: The Father does not need his children to return to him what he gives them. Instead, they can pass that love and service on to their fellows and to the evolving Supreme Being. In time we may begin to reveal the Supreme to our fellows, and we can enlarge that revelation as we ascend. Letting the grace we have received flow on to the person beside us is itself a way of taking part in the growth of God.
p056.s6.h: IX. Universal Absolute Unity — All Converges on the Father
p056.s6.b0: This section takes up the great philosophic question of the master universe: does the Absolute come before the Trinity, or the Trinity before the Absolute? The author says that the eternity of the Trinity invalidates any conclusion that makes the Absolute the ancestor of all things. The Absolute is the Trinity’s impersonal reaction to basic space situations, and when we follow the question to its end, we return to the Universal I AM, the Paradise Father.
p056.s6.b1: The most beautiful promise is that at the end of every quest we meet the same One. Whether we attain God the Sevenfold, comprehend God the Supreme, or find God the Ultimate, at the close of each adventure we will rediscover, on a new level of experience, the Father of all personalities.
p056.s7.h: X. Truth, Beauty, and Goodness — and Love
p056.s7.b0: On worlds settled in light and life, the chief pursuit of mortals is the comprehensible elements of Deity: truth, beauty, and goodness. Truth is the basis of science and philosophy and the intellectual foundation of religion; beauty sponsors art, music, and the rhythms of life; goodness embraces ethics, morality, and religion. Beauty is the unification of contrasts, and its height is the drama of man finding God and God finding man.

head: Element of cosmologic thought
Content
rows: Hunger for harmony and thirst for beauty
Love of the beautiful and appreciation of the artistic touch in all creation
From the realization of truth to divine goodness and God-consciousness

p056.s7.b2: Standing opposite unity is sin. Every impulse of electron, thought, or spirit acts within the whole, but sin alone is isolated, resisting gravity on the levels of mind and spirit. That is why antisocial self-realization is potentially evil, and why cosmic socialization is the highest form of personality unification.
p056.s7.b4: The paper also calls materialism and atheism the maximation of ugliness. If beauty is what binds variety into one, then a worldview that severs everything from its source stands at the opposite extreme. Goodness is similar: recognizing goodness is not enough; actually possessing goodness—greatness—is the measure of real divinity attainment.
p056.s7.b5: When truth, beauty, and goodness are expressed in the life of a God-knowing person, they bear the fruits of divinity: intellectual peace, social progress, moral satisfaction, spiritual joy, and cosmic wisdom. And the sum of these three qualities is love. All of Part II ends, finally, with one very short sentence.
p056.s8.b0: Paper 56 gathers a vast cosmology into the simplest conclusion. The universe is one, God is one in power and personality, and all beings converge on the Paradise Father. In the evolving universes that unity is not a given fact but an achievement in progress, and each person’s unified personality and love for others become part of that achievement. With this paper Part II closes, and Part III turns to the history of Urantia.

p057.lead: From a force organizer’s report 987 billion years ago to the inland seas waiting for life: the long story of how our planet was born.

p057.foot.text: Presented by a Life Carrier, a member of the original Urantia Corps and now a resident observer

p057.s0.h: Introduction — Why Read a Planet’s Family Tree?
p057.s0.b0: Paper 57 opens Part III of The Urantia Book, “The History of Urantia.” Its author is a Life Carrier, a member of the original Urantia Corps, who draws on the archives of Jerusem to tell the story of our planet’s origin. The narrative begins with the birth of a nebula and ends with seas made ready for the planting of life.
p057.s0.b1: The author first explains how he will handle dates. The records hold exact years, but he does not give them; he uses the nearest whole numbers instead, and he reckons backward from the early decades of the twentieth century of the Christian era. The figures in this paper are therefore best read not as a precise timetable but as milestones marking a vast movement.
p057.s0.b2: Although it is written in the language of astronomy and geology, the paper leaves a feeling that is deeply religious. The ground beneath our feet is no stray lump of rock that happened to roll into place. It is a sphere shaped, through hundreds of billions of years of preparation and supervision, into a home ready to welcome life.
p057.s1.h: I. The Andronover Nebula — The Work of the Force Organizers
p057.s1.b0: Urantia came from our sun, and our sun is one of the many offspring of the Andronover nebula. That nebula, in turn, took its origin in the universal force-charge of space in the superuniverse of Orvonton. Yet the first scene of the story features not stars but persons. A force organizer reports that space conditions are favorable, a permit is issued, and the organizer and his staff set out on a long journey.

p057.s1.b2: What deserves our attention is what happens after the initiation. Once the revolutions begin, the living force organizers withdraw at right angles to the plane of the revolving disk, and from then on the inherent qualities of energy ensure an orderly evolution. Creation begins with the touch of personality, but afterward it grows of itself according to the laws placed within it.
p057.s2.h: II–IV. The Four Lives of a Nebula — From Circular Cloud to Sun Dispersion
p057.s2.b0: Every evolving material creation is born of a circular, gaseous nebula, and Andronover followed that path. At first it was an enormous gas cloud shaped somewhat like a flattened spheroid. After reaching its maximum of mass it began to contract and spin faster and faster, until it became a spiral nebula with two great arms. When its rotation reached the critical point, suns began to be thrown off into independent orbits.

p057.s2.b3: In the middle of this physical chronicle a spiritual event takes place. Scarcely a million years after the recaptive period began, Michael of Nebadon, a Creator Son, chose this disintegrating nebula as the site of his adventure in universe building. The architectural worlds of Salvington were begun, and by about 200 billion years ago some cooled planets had become ready for life implantation; the oldest inhabited worlds of Nebadon date from those times.
p057.s2.b4: Our sun was born near the end of this long history. It was the fifty-sixth from the last of the Andronover second solar family, and the suns and sun systems that came from the nebula number 1,013,628 in all. The nebula itself no longer exists, but it lives on in its offspring.
p057.s3.h: V. Origin of Monmatia — The Visit of Angona
p057.s3.b0: The solar system was not born in the usual way. The young sun was a variable star whose brightness rose and fell in cycles of three and one-half days, and this pulsation made it highly responsive to outside influences. Just then, 4.5 billion years ago, the Angona system approached; at its center was a dark giant of space, solid, highly charged, and possessing tremendous gravity pull. Planetary systems born this way are rare: fewer than one per cent of those in Orvonton.
p057.s3.b2: When Angona made its closest approach, the sun underwent a partial disruption, and a vast column of solar gases—pointed at both ends and bulging at the center—was drawn away. That column became the ancestor of the twelve planets. Gas thrown off from the opposite side later condensed into meteors and space dust. Angona drew the material away, but it did not take any of it for itself.

head: Part of the gas column
What it became
rows: The five inner and five outer planets, which soon solidified and grew by capturing meteors

p057.s3.b4: Another trace of this origin is that the planets do not circle the sun in its equatorial plane; they travel in a plane set at a considerable angle to it. Retrograde motion, we are told, is always accidental and appears only in systems containing masses of diverse origin. Even a small irregularity in the sky holds the memory of a long history.
p057.s4.h: VI. The Solar System Stage — The Planet-Forming Era
p057.s4.b0: The planets did not stop growing once the solar system had formed. The condensing nuclei of the ten planets took shape, smaller satellites merged, and by 3 billion years ago the solar system was functioning much as it does today. About this time it was placed on the physical registry of Nebadon and given the name Monmatia. Every planet and satellite is still growing by capturing meteors.
p057.s4.b1: This section explains the power of tides in some detail. Tidal friction slows rotation until one face is always turned toward the larger body, as with Mercury and the moon; and a smaller body that comes within two and one-half times the radius of a larger one is torn apart. Saturn’s rings are the remains of a shattered satellite, and the asteroids are the fragments of an ancient fifth planet that came too close to Jupiter. In the far future, the moon too will be drawn near the earth and meet a similar fate.
p057.s5.h: VII. The Meteoric Era — The Volcanic Age — A Planet of Fire
p057.s5.b0: With no atmosphere to protect it, the young planet was struck directly by meteors, and its heavier elements sank toward the center. By 2 billion years ago Urantia had grown large enough to hold a primitive atmosphere, and definite volcanic action began. Later the whole earth became a veritable fiery inferno. Yet even then a crust of comparatively light granite was quietly forming.
p057.s5.b2: The primitive atmosphere held water vapor, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, and hydrogen chloride, but little or no free oxygen. As it cooled, rain began to fall, and for thousands of years a vast blanket of steam covered the planet so that the sun never shone on its surface. Oxygen built up in significant quantities only after seaweeds and other plant life appeared. The author also notes that the radioactive materials open to our study come from the surface and are relatively recent acquisitions, so every estimate of the planet’s age by the radium clock is too short.
p057.s5.b3: The author adds that all this violent activity is a normal part of making an evolutionary world of the Urantia type. Collision and destruction, capture and growth are not signs of disorder; they are the astronomic preliminaries to the life adventures of time. Some 2.5 billion years ago Urantia had only about one tenth of its present mass, but it was growing rapidly by taking in meteors. The passage reminds us that a process that looks like chaos may, within a larger purpose, be a time of preparation.
p057.s6.h: VIII. Crustal Stabilization and the First Continent — Seas Waiting for Life
p057.s6.b0: One billion years ago marks the actual beginning of Urantia history. The planet had reached about its present size and was placed on the physical registries of Nebadon under the name Urantia. As the crust cooled, the first ocean formed: a world-wide covering of fresh, not salty, water, averaging more than a mile deep. Then the floor of the Pacific sank, and the first continent rose from the world ocean.
p057.s6.b1: Administrative preparation moved forward side by side with the physical. The section carefully records how one small sphere was entered, step by step, in the records of the universe.

p057.s6.b4: From 800 million years ago, the land rose until almost a third of the earth’s surface was one continental body, and the first climatic differences appeared. When the continent began to break apart 750 million years ago, the ocean pushed into the land as long fingerlike seas, forming shallow waters and sheltered bays; by 650 million years ago those waters were nearing the saltiness essential to life. These inland seas would later write the record of life on pages of stone.
p057.s7.b0: Paper 57 is crowded with numbers, but what they point to is a single quality: patience. More than eight hundred billion years passed between the force organizer’s initiation of the nebula and the inland seas reaching the saltiness life requires. Along the way Michael chose this nebula as the site of his universe, and a small, insignificant sphere was entered in the registries, destined to become the “⟦Q 57:8.6⟧world of the cross.⟦/Q⟧” Our own lives, too, unfold on a stage that was prepared over a very long time.

p057.s7.b2: Paper 58 tells how the Life Carriers planted life in the seas prepared here—the life establishment on Urantia. If we keep in mind the conditions of atmosphere, ocean, and continent described in this paper, we will better understand why the time and place of life implantation were chosen as they were.
p058.lead: Salt seas and an ozone shield, drifting continents and records written in stone: how the Life Carriers prepared Urantia for life and planted it.

p058.foot.text: Presented by a member of the Urantia Life Carrier Corps now resident on the planet

p058.s0.h: Introduction — A Planet Where Experiment Was Allowed
p058.s0.b0: If Paper 57 showed how the body of the planet was formed, Paper 58 tells how life took hold upon it. The author is a member of the Life Carrier Corps still resident on this planet. He begins by explaining what kind of world Urantia is: in all Satania there are only sixty-one life-modification planets like ours.
p058.s0.b1: On most inhabited worlds life is placed according to established techniques, and the Life Carriers have little leeway. But about one world in ten is designated a decimal planet, and there they are permitted to experiment in an effort to modify or improve the standard types of living beings. Urantia is such a planet, which is why life here has its own distinctive character.

p058.s1.h: I. Physical-Life Prerequisites — Waiting for Salt Water
p058.s1.b0: Six hundred million years ago a commission of Life Carriers from Jerusem arrived to study Urantia’s physical conditions. The principle they started from is clear. Life Carriers cannot initiate life until a sphere is ripe for it, and they cannot make life develop faster than the physical progress of the planet can support.
p058.s1.b1: The Satania Life Carriers had projected a sodium chloride pattern of life, so they had to wait until the ocean had become salty enough. The commission returned to Jerusem to await the further breakup of the continent, which would create more inland seas and sheltered bays. Those shallow seas, through which sunlight could reach the bottom, offered the ideal conditions for life implantation.
p058.s1.b3: This passage also tells us something about our own bodies. Our primitive ancestors swam in the salty ocean; today a similar salt solution circulates in our blood stream, bathing every cell. In a sense we carry within us the sea in which life first began.
p058.s2.h: II. The Urantia Atmosphere — More Than Two-Score Protections
p058.s2.b0: The atmosphere is life’s protective covering. The ozone layer, which begins about ten miles above the surface, would be only one tenth of an inch thick at surface conditions, yet it shields us from destructive ultraviolet radiation. Were it just a trifle thicker, it would also block the health-giving ultraviolet rays we need. At night the blanketing effect of the air keeps heat from escaping too quickly.
p058.s2.b1: The author uses this delicate balance to answer mechanistic interpretations. The Urantia midwayers have gathered more than fifty thousand facts of physics and chemistry that they believe show intelligent purpose in the material creation. And there are more than two-score “fortuitous” protective operations similar to the ozone layer.

p058.s2.b4: The section goes on to explain sunspots and auroras, the daily variation of the compass, and the conducting layers that reflect radio waves. Sunspots are solar cyclones whirling in opposite directions above and below the sun’s equator, and their magnetic fields hurl charged particles to the earth’s outer atmosphere, producing the auroras. The passage shows that the phenomena of the sky form one connected system.
p058.s3.h: III. Spatial Environment — Life Unshaken by the Short Space Rays
p058.s3.b0: Space is flooded with short space rays pouring from vast hydrogen clouds and blazing nebulae. This short-ray energy charge is four hundred times greater than all other forms of radiant energy in organized space. The great hydrogen clouds are veritable cosmic chemical laboratories, holding every phase of evolving energy and changing matter.
p058.s3.b1: Yet all this tremendous energy activity does not alter the inheritance factors of the germ plasm. It belongs to the environment needed for establishing life, but the implanted life is fully resistant to the flood. And these cosmic conditions, too, had to reach a favorable stage before the Life Carriers could begin their work.
p058.s4.h: IV. The Life-Dawn Era — Three Marine Implantations
p058.s4.b0: The author first corrects a misunderstanding. Despite their name, the Life Carriers did not bring life to Urantia. Life here was formulated on the planet itself, and no other world in all Nebadon has a life existence just like ours.
p058.s4.b2: Five hundred fifty million years ago the Life Carrier corps, in co-operation with spiritual powers and superphysical forces, organized the original life patterns and planted them in the waters. The implantation was made in three places at once, out of foresight: as the continents separated, each great land mass would carry life with it in its warm seas. All planetary life down to the days of Caligastia came from these three implantations.
p058.s4.b5: And indeed, by 500 million years ago marine plant life was well established and the continents were already separating. Greenland and the arctic lands, with North and South America, began their slow westward drift; Africa moved slightly south, forming the trough of the Mediterranean basin; and Antarctica, Australia, and the Pacific islands broke away to the south and east. The Life Carriers’ foresight proved exactly right.
p058.s5.h: V. The Continental Drift — Land Floating on a Sea of Basalt
p058.s5.b0: The earth’s core is as dense and rigid as steel, and at the center its temperature is slightly above that of the sun’s surface. The outer thousand miles consist mainly of rock; the heavy metals sank deep when the planet was molten. The outer crust, about forty miles thick, rests on a layer of molten basalt, and the continents still float on this cushiony sea.
p058.s5.b1: The continents stay above water because the sea bottoms are made of denser basalt. Continental pressure at the level of the ocean floor is about 20,000 pounds per square inch, while the water pressure on the ocean floor is only about 5,000 pounds, so every continent tends to creep toward the sea. Earthquakes, the author adds, are caused not by volcanoes but by the sliding and shifting of the solid outer crust.
p058.s5.b2: Figures for density support the explanation. Urantia’s average density is a little more than five and one-half times that of water; granite is less than three times as dense, and the core twelve times. In the prelife ages the sinking ocean floor thrust up a single continent, whose fringes then slid toward the Pacific; ever since, the eastern coast of the ancient Asiatic continent has hovered over the precipice of the ocean depths.
p058.s6.h: VI. The Transition Period — From Plant to Animal
p058.s6.b0: Four hundred fifty million years ago the transition from vegetable to animal life took place. This development was inherent in the original life patterns and came about gradually; even today the transition slime molds can hardly be classified as either plants or animals. But between the great divisions of the animal kingdom, and between the highest prehuman animals and the dawn men, no connecting links will be found.
p058.s6.b2: New species do not arise from the slow accumulation of small variations; they appear suddenly as full-fledged new orders of life. At the same time the author makes clear that this is wholly biologic and strictly natural. The section also distinguishes between body and mind.

p058.s6.b5: Life moves through endless cycles of gains and losses, adjustments and readjustments, as it strives to fit an ever-changing environment. Organisms that attain cosmic unity persist; those that fall short cease to exist. This observation—that life never stops adapting—applies just as well to the way we live.
p058.s7.h: VII. The Geologic History Book — A Story Written in Stone
p058.s7.b0: The rocks of the life-dawn era lie at or near the surface over about one eighth of today’s land area, holding fossils of algae, corallike plants, primitive Protozoa, and spongelike transition organisms. The rocks around Lake Superior and in the Grand Canyon are especially easy to interpret, and the St. Croix valley of Wisconsin records one hundred and twenty-seven successive lava flows.
p058.s7.b1: These strata also foreshadow the age to come. Dark shales and slates in some upper layers contain organic carbon, witnessing to the ancestors of the plants that would overrun the earth in the coal age. The lava flows of the era brought iron, copper, and lead near the surface, and some of the iron mines of North America and Europe lie in the rocks of these transition periods.
p058.s7.b2: By the end of this era marine life had spread through all the waters of the world, and the floors of the shallow inland seas were covered with luxuriant vegetation. The whole story remains in the fossil pages of the stone book, which tell the truth to anyone who learns the skill of reading them.
p058.s8.b0: Paper 58 shows that life did not arise by accident. It was planted according to a plan that waited for the right time, studied conditions carefully, and looked far into the future. The Life Carriers waited for the seas to become salty, and foreseeing the breakup of the continents, they planted life in three places. Yet what followed unfolded within natural law, and mind was given as a gift from above.

p058.s8.b2: Paper 59 follows the life planted in the seas through hundreds of millions of years, era by era, as it flourishes and finally comes up onto the land—the marine-life era. With this paper’s three implantation areas and drifting continents in mind, we can picture that long chronicle almost like a map.
p059.lead: From trilobites to fishes and frogs, and on to the age of biologic tribulation: the 250 million years in which the sea mothered the life of our world.

p059.foot.text: Presented by a Life Carrier of Nebadon, one of the original corps assigned to Urantia

p059.s0.h: Introduction — A Quarter of the Planet’s History
p059.s0.b0: Paper 59 is a Life Carrier’s chronicle of the marine-life era. The author begins by dividing Urantia’s history of about one billion years into five major eras, giving for each the name used by geologists. The marine-life era treated in this paper is the third of them, and it covers about one quarter of the planet’s history.
p059.s0.b2: The marine-life era is further divided into six long periods, each marked by well-defined developments in both geology and biology. As the era opens, the sea bottoms and continental shelves are already covered with abundant vegetation, and simple animals have spread along the coast lines until the inland seas teem with life. The author describes this as the moment when the opening chapters of the great “stone book” of life’s record are about to be written.
p059.s0.b3: North America serves as an especially good textbook for this chronicle. The continent is wonderfully rich in fossil-bearing deposits from the whole marine-life era, and its oldest layers are clearly set apart from the preceding period by extensive erosion deposits. That is why North American place names appear so often in this paper.
p059.s1.h: I. Early Marine Life in the Shallow Seas — The Trilobite Age
p059.s1.b0: By 400 million years ago marine life, both plant and animal, was well distributed over the whole world, and the climate grew warmer and more even. Vegetation for the first time crawled out onto the land. And then, with no gradual line of ancestors, the first multicellular animals appeared: the trilobites.
p059.s1.b2: Trilobites were poor swimmers; they floated sluggishly or crawled along the sea bottom, curling up for protection when attacked. They developed into four groups—carnivorous, herbivorous, omnivorous, and “mud eaters”—and the last group’s ability to live largely on inorganic matter explains its great increase and long survival. Traces of the three original implantations also remain: the early animals of the Western Hemisphere differed slightly from those of Eurasia and Australasia. Geologists call this period the Cambrian.

p059.s1.b4: The world climate in these times was oceanic, not continental. There were no great ice sheets, and the warm southern seas reached north to the polar regions. The Gulf Stream flowed across central North America and turned east to warm the shores of Greenland, making that now ice-covered land a veritable tropic paradise. The passage reminds us not to judge the past by today’s map.
p059.s2.h: II. The First Continental Flood Stage — The Invertebrate-Animal Age
p059.s2.b0: From 350 million years ago every continent except central Asia was flooded again and again. These risings and sinkings were gradual and undramatic, and the Asiatic mother continent followed a course of its own, becoming in recent ages the most stable of all land masses. The almost lone exception to this quiet time was the great eruption in eastern Kentucky some 330 million years ago.
p059.s2.b1: This was the great age of individual animal evolution, when every type of life below the vertebrates appears in the fossils. The ancestors of corals, jellyfish, cephalopods, and many other forms flourished. But apart from a few burrowing worms there were still no land animals, because the air held too much carbon dioxide. Geologists know this period as the Ordovician.
p059.s2.b3: The trilobites were still prominent, existing in tens of thousands of patterns and serving as the forerunners of modern crustaceans; some had from twenty-five to four thousand tiny eyes. But by the end of the period they shared the seas with other invertebrates, and early in the next period they perished entirely. Even a form of life that dominates an age does not stay forever.
p059.s3.h: III. The Second Great Flood Stage — The Coral Period — The Brachiopod Age
p059.s3.b0: Three hundred million years ago another great submergence began. The seas teemed with lime-shelled life, laying down the first widespread limestone deposit, about a thousand feet thick on average. The deposits of this age hold much gas, oil, zinc, lead, and rock salt; the gas and oil came from plants and animals of the submerged lands. The rock over which Niagara Falls now flows also dates from this time.
p059.s3.b1: By 290 million years ago the sea had largely withdrawn, and early mountain building began on every continent. The greatest of these upheavals were the Himalayas of Asia and the great Caledonian Mountains, stretching from Ireland through Scotland to Spitzbergen. Violent eruptions followed in Europe, leaving alternating layers of lava and rock 25,000 feet thick in the region of the British Isles.
p059.s3.b2: The trilobites declined rapidly, and cephalopods growing to fifteen feet long suddenly appeared and became masters of the seas. By the end of the epoch the seas were so salty that little life survived. Then, after the primitive water scorpions, true scorpions—the first real air breathers—suddenly appeared. This period is the Silurian.
p059.s4.h: IV. The Great Land-Emergence Stage — The Age of Fishes
p059.s4.b0: For long ages the sea had held the upper hand, but now a time of land victory arrived. By 270 million years ago all the continents were above water, and the bare landscape was being clothed in green. The fern family suddenly appeared and spread everywhere, and leafless trees formed forests a hundred feet tall.
p059.s4.b2: The greatest event of the age was the sudden appearance of the fishes. Vertebrates appeared 250 million years ago, descended from modified arthropods. Some toothed fishes reached twenty-five to thirty feet in length, and today’s sharks are their survivors. This period, called the Devonian, lasted almost fifty million years.
p059.s4.b4: As the land rose, North America was joined to Europe by land bridges reaching to Greenland, and Greenland still holds the remains of these early land plants beneath its ice. Volcanic activity in the St. Lawrence region 230 million years ago left Mount Royal at Montreal, and the Susquehanna River exposes over 13,000 feet of this epoch’s layers.
p059.s5.h: V. The Crustal-Shifting Stage — The Fern-Forest Carboniferous Period — The Age of Frogs
p059.s5.b0: The appearance of fish was the high point of marine evolution; from here on, the evolution of land life grows ever more important. When the seas were at their height, about 210 million years ago, the first land animals suddenly appeared: air-breathing amphibians developed from arthropods whose swim bladders had become lungs. Snails, scorpions, and frogs crawled out of the sea onto the land, and insects soon spread over the continents.
p059.s5.b3: Coal is the water-preserved and pressure-modified remains of the rank vegetation of bogs and swamp shores. Tree roots remain in the clay beneath coal beds just as they grew, proving that coal formed exactly where it is found. Each time the land sank and rose a new layer was laid down, so the number of coal layers records the number of those movements.

p059.s5.b5: The Carboniferous closed 180 million years ago as eastern North America rose, marking the beginning of the modern Appalachian and western mountains. The rising land began to replace the mild marine climate with a less mild, more variable continental one. The spore-bearing Carboniferous trees were often seven feet across and one hundred and twenty-five feet high, and modern ferns are relics of that vanished age.
p059.s6.h: VI. The Climatic Transition Stage — The Age of Biologic Tribulation
p059.s6.b0: The last period of the marine-life era was a time of great impoverishment of life. Its cause was not the cooling of the crust or volcanic activity, but an unusual combination of ordinary influences: shrinking seas and rising lands. The mild oceanic climate disappeared, harsh continental weather took its place, and two new climatic factors appeared—glaciation and aridity.
p059.s6.b2: Yet this ordeal was not an ending but a sifting. Seed plants appeared for the first time, giving land animals a better food supply, and insects evolved resting stages to survive winter and drought. Frogs held on in drying pools and, in Africa, took the first step toward becoming reptiles. Marine animals sheltered in three refuges and later went forth from them as new species, born of adversity, to replenish the seas.

p059.s6.b4: The end of this Permian period is also the end of the Paleozoic, an era of two hundred and fifty million years. The sea nurtured life through the long ages when the land could not support it, and now it gives up that role as the second stage of evolution begins on land.
p059.s7.b0: Paper 59 tells how life climbed upward step by step through what looks like a tedious repetition of floods and uplifts. New orders of life appeared suddenly in age after age, and at the end came a trial that cut more than a hundred thousand species down to fewer than five hundred. Yet that trial left behind the forms with survival value to become the ancestors of the next age. Hardship can be a preparation rather than an end; this is the deepest lesson the paper leaves.
